reasoning_traces.think:
BPS synthesizes predictive densities through a supra-Bayesian framework that integrates outcome-dependent weights, cross-model dependence, and time-varying discounting. It avoids degeneration to a single model by incorporating a baseline safe-haven density. The synthesis function α(y|x) operates via Jeffrey’s rule rather than Bayes’ theorem, enabling density recalibration without explicit likelihood evaluation. Outcome-dependent weights ωj(xj) allow models to be trusted more where they perform well, while cross-model dependence adjusts weights based on joint latent states. Time-varying synthesis uses discount factors to reflect evolving uncertainty, modeled via Gibbs sampling and variational Bayes. This approach ensures robustness against model misspecification and improves forecast accuracy compared to standard Bayesian model averaging.
